notes:
Circuit: a 4-column L/C ladder against a right-hand stack of five sources. Six horizontal rails (y ~30 top, ~188, ~388, ~575, ~760, ~913 bottom) are spanned by five vertical columns (x ~95, ~285, ~440, ~620, ~810). The right column is a chain V-AC(3V 1kHz) / I-AC(5A 1kHz) / V-DC(5V) / I-DC(10A) / V-DC(15V) linking consecutive rails; each left column carries one inductor then one capacitor. 14 components, 7 nets.

THE DECIDING OBSERVATION: this drafter uses two mutually exclusive notations, both of which appear many times on this one sheet, so essentially every site is decidable from ink alone. (a) A fat filled solder blob, ~10-11 px across against 3-4 px strokes, means CONNECTED - e.g. S27 at (283,577) is a blob spanning rows 573-580, x 276-287. (b) A sideways jog - the column steps ~12 px sideways over ~35 px of travel, carries itself across the rail displaced, then steps back - means NOT CONNECTED; e.g. S26 at (422,577), pixel-verified: the column runs at x=435 down to row 562, walks left to x=423 by row 576, crosses the rail at rows 577-578 with no thickening at all, then walks back to x=435 by row 590. I applied this rule uniformly and checked the blob/jog character of every CRITICAL site in the crops, plus S26, S27, S10 and the S11/S15 pair in raw pixels.

S5 (847,131) and S16 (315,285) sit inside the handwritten '1 kHz' and '5 uH' labels and are left at the default; they touch no terminal.

SITE DECISIONS - CROSSINGS (sideways jog). Four the tracer already had right and I confirmed: S10 (414,187) column 3 past rail 2; S13 (272,194) column 2 past rail 2; S18 (599,386) column 4 past rail 3; S30 (604,760) column 4 past rail 5. Four I OVERRODE, all of which the tracer defaulted to junction:
  S11 (593,190) + S15 (605,206) - one single jog (column 4 past rail 2) that the skeletoniser split across two sites, so neither 'junction' nor 'crossing' can express it. Used explicit edge groups: S11 = [[8,16,25,27,29],[18,22]] - e8 the column arriving from the top rail, e16 the upper half of the jog, e25 the lower half, e27 the short lead-out stub, e29 the column continuing down to S18; e18 and e22 the two halves of rail 2 - and S15 = "none" so the second site adds nothing. Left as junction this shorted the top rail to rail 2.
  S19 (419,390) - column 3 past rail 3; explicit groups [[28,42],[38,40]] (column above/below, rail left/right). Junction would have put the 10uH's top on rail 3 instead of the top rail and shorted the two together.
  S25 (611,574) - column 4 past rail 4; explicit groups [[48,54],[50,51]].
  S26 (422,577) - column 3 past rail 4; explicit groups [[49,56],[51,52]]. Junction would have shorted the 10uH/50uF midpoint (n4) into net 0.
  I used explicit edge groups rather than the 'crossing' keyword at these four because the jog geometry leaves the two column stubs only ~90 deg apart rather than opposite, so an automatic opposite-branch pairing is not safe. Consequence of the tracer's original all-junction reading: 22 of the 27 terminals collapsed onto one net.

THE ONE GENUINELY UNCERTAIN POINT - rail 5's right end (799,758) vs the right column at (806,760). The drafter drew a small HOLLOW pen loop on the right column exactly where rail 5 arrives, but the rail's ink stops 5-6 px short of it (pixel dump rows 758-760: ink out to x=799-800, then clean paper to x=804, then the loop). I left it unconnected - i.e. I did not add a bridge or a merge - for two independent reasons. (1) Ink: every connection this drafter actually made is a fat FILLED blob (S9, S12, S20, S27, S31, S34, S35, S37); this is a hollow curl with a real gap. (2) Electrics: rail 5 is already part of net 0 (the x~440 column runs from the S31 blob straight down to the S37 blob on the bottom rail), and the bottom rail is net 0 too, so bridging this gap would place BOTH terminals of V-DC #11 (15V) on net 0 - a dead short across a voltage source - and would short I-DC #9 (10A) as well. Rule 1 forbids that reading. Left open, the 10A source and the 15V source sit in series in a loop from net 0 back to net 0 via n6, which is degenerate but legal and is what the ink supports. If a reviewer reads that loop as a real contact, the single edit would be merge [["9.1","11.0"]]-style bridging of n6 into 0.
  Related, and flagged deliberately: because the drafter blobbed BOTH S27/S35 and S31/S37, rail 4, rail 5 and the bottom rail are genuinely one net in this drawing. I checked all four of those sites in raw pixels; every one is an unmistakable filled blob with the column continuing through, so this is what is drawn, not a tracing artefact - even though it makes the 5V source's return and the 10A source's top share ground with everything else.

CLASSES: all 14 symbols match their labels - inductors 1uH/5uH/10uH/50uH, capacitors 5uF/10uF/50uF/100uF, V-AC 3V 1kHz (circle with a sine), I-AC 5A 1kHz (circle with a sine over an arrow), V-DC 5V and V-DC 15V (circles with +/- bars), I-DC 10A (circle with an up arrow), and GND. No reclassification.

GAP BRIDGES: 5 reported, all inside label glyphs ('1 kHz', '5 uH') or between the two halves of the split S11/S15 jog; none changes the netlist and none was dropped.
